Subject: High p95 latency + elevated 5xx — seeing customer impact

Hi Lauren / Priyom,

We’re seeing sustained spikes in p95 latency and a jump in 5xx errors on the production inference route for our Medella integration. Key metrics right now: p50 ~ 320ms (normal), p95 ~ 2.2s (was ~420ms), and 5xx error rate ~4.5% across the last 15m. Throughput looks flattened — client-side queuing has increased.

This is impacting downstream ingestion (claims classification) and a handful of customer transactions are timing out. I’ve attached a small diagnostic export (logs + traces) that shows repeated KV cache misses and a tight burst of long sequences.

Can Redwood put an elevated response on this? We need an exec-level contact and a war-room/standby while we stabilize. Tom and I are available immediately; we’d like visibility into rollback/fallback plans and estimated time to restore p95 under 700ms.

Attachments: diagnostic-logs-20261201.tar.gz

Thanks — Sara
Sara Khan
Head of Integrations, Medella Health

War-room notes / actions taken (08:40–08:47 PT):
- Enabled emergency autoscale for Medella tenant (+35% GPU pool; policy: immediate burst, will scale down automatically).
- Routed 30% of new inference requests to q4_8bit variant (fallback model) and enabled synchronous streaming to minimize client-side buffering.
- Triggered a lightweight canary rollback for the most recent model build on the affected route; telemetry sent to the bridge.
- Uploaded the initial SLO violation report (slo-violation-report.pdf) to the drive link.

Current telemetry (08:47): p95 -> 1.1s, 5xx -> 2.1%. Still above target but trending down. Next: confirm whether cache warm-up or a kernel path regression is responsible. Maria (SRE) is running targeted KV cache metrics.

Attachments: playbook-standby.docx (ops checklist we followed)

-David

Date: 2026-12-01T11:12:00-08:00
Subject: Status update: telemetry & customer impact (11:12 PT)

Quick status (telemetry snapshot at 11:10 PT):
- p95: 560ms (down from 2.2s peak)
- p50: 340ms
- 5xx error rate: 0.85%
- Throughput: at 92% of normal while autoscale remains active

Root cause signals: KV cache miss storm during high-concurrency bursts combined with a subtle kernel selector regression under sequences > 1,500 tokens. Cache priming + routing to q4_8bit reduced tail latency. We’ve scheduled a temporary kernel roll-forward to the previous selection logic for the affected route (deploy window: 15m, will be monitored).

Action items:
1) Keep fallback model routing and autoscale for the next 90m.
2) SRE to produce a short runbook for Medella engineers describing safe retry/backoff patterns.
3) Product to open a ticket for kernel selector and quantify regression risk across other tenants.
4) CS (Lauren) to confirm external comms and proposed service credit.

Sara / Tom — apologies for the disruption and thank you for rapid signal sharing. We’ll keep the 30-minute update cadence until we hit our target.

-Monica Patel
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
